clue.text: Scholarly Scot, he's in the ra

parts.note: scholarly means academic, as in an academic approach
Ian is a typically Scottish first name, so a Scot is IAN in crosswords

explanation.surface: A learned Scotsman has been elected to the Royal Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: The RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London; its members carry this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Academy is formally called by this title, so 'he's in the RA' describes one.

clue.text: Secretly assured individual colleague

parts.note: assured means self-confident, sure of oneself
individual, a single one, is I, the Roman numeral one
a colleague is an ally, someone on your side

explanation.surface: A self-confident lone colleague is up to something on the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in private, told in trust and not to be spread, is doing it on the quiet.

clue.text: Expletive from driver at the end

indicators.note: from here takes just the first and last letters of the word driver, its outside pair

parts.note: taken as written, placed at the end as the clue says

explanation.surface: A motorist swears as the journey ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' tells you AT goes after the first and last letters of 'driver'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild oath of annoyance, like 'blast' or 'damn', is an expletive.

clue.text: Come in struggling after heartless maiden produced memory aid

indicators.note: after says the shuffled letters come behind the letters from maiden
heartless removes the middle of the word maiden, leaving only its first and last letters
struggling suggests the words come in thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl came in fighting and somehow produced a way to remember things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' suggests a girl, but only its first and last letters count; 'struggling' signals the shuffle of 'Come in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme or acronym used to help remember facts is a device for recall, a memory aid.

clue.text: Produce note inside box

indicators.note: inside says the note sits within the letters for box

parts.note: a crate is a box for transporting goods
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A piece of paper is found tucked into a box.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something into being is to make or produce it.

clue.text: Anthony's workers

parts.note: Ant is a pet form of Anthony, so the possessive reads as small insects, and the worker caste of a colony does the labour

explanation.walkthrough: Worker is the name for the sterile labouring caste in an insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects whose colonies rely on sterile labourers are known for their worker caste.

clue.text: Where diplomats get good percentage?

parts.note: a good mark or price is a high one
a commission is a percentage paid to an agent on a sale

explanation.surface: Asks where embassy staff receive a generous cut.
explanation.walkthrough: A high commission is the embassy one Commonwealth country keeps in another.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplomatic mission of one Commonwealth country in another is the office where its envoys work.

clue.text: Again come round with nearly everything relating to one who is self-centred

definitions.text: relating to one who is self-centred

indicators.note: come round suggests the letters turn about into a new order
nearly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: Again someone comes round bringing almost everything, all about themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come round' reads as a visit, but 'round' shuffles 'Again come'; 'nearly' trims the last letter from the word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for a person obsessed with their own importance describes a self-centred one.

clue.text: He proposes to put it on a lady's finger

definitions.text: He proposes to put it on a lady's finger

parts.words: He proposes to put it on a lady's finger
parts.note: a man making a marriage proposal plans to slip a piece of jewellery onto the woman's hand

explanation.definitionFit: A man asking for a woman's hand offers a band to wear on her finger as a sign of betrothal.

clue.text: Not a community person

parts.note: the community is the European Community, and this person is against it rather than unsociable

explanation.walkthrough: The European Community was the earlier name of the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed to greater European union is hostile to the European Community.

clue.text: University gets wrong mark from computer's multi-user operating system

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A university gets a cross mark from its computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating system developed at Bell Labs lets many people use one computer at once.

clue.text: Twosome went round circular stall

indicators.note: went round says the letters for twosome surround the circular letter

parts.note: a twosome is both of a pair
O is circular in shape

explanation.surface: A couple walked around a round market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosed stand at a market or fair is a kind of stall.

clue.text: Arkwright's son coming from southern border

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A son of the industrialist Arkwright comes from the southern border.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright suggests Richard Arkwright the inventor, but here it is Noah, who built the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah built the Ark, and one of his three sons in Genesis bears this name.

clue.text: Fine line bearing natural aptitude

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
bearing, one's manner or demeanour, is one's air

explanation.surface: A neat line of posture shows a natural talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural talent or knack for something is an inborn aptitude.

clue.text: Insert in song

parts.note: taken as written
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Asks for something to be slipped into a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of material set into a surface as decoration is an insert.

clue.text: Produced too many eggs that had been put on top of other things

definitions.meaning: a hen that laid too many eggs ...

definitions.text: that had been put on top of other things
definitions.meaning: covered with a layer placed above

explanation.definitionFit: Laying excessively and having been covered with a layer are both senses of the past tense of placing over.

clue.text: Some gentlemen jointly order with authority

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several men acting together give a formal command.
explanation.definitionFit: To command or prescribe something formally is to order it with authority.

clue.text: Orchestral compositions at one time right in channel islands

indicators.note: in says the other pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

explanation.surface: Old orchestral pieces were once rightly placed in the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British islands such as Jersey and Guernsey off the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces for a solo instrument with orchestra are plural works in this Italian form.

clue.text: Bloomer from Felix's family

parts.note: Felix is the famous cartoon cat, so his family is the cat family
kin means family

explanation.surface: A gaffe made by one of Felix the cat's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a thing that blooms, a flower spike.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of flowers on a willow or hazel blooms in spring, so it is a bloomer.

clue.text: I am to axe peculiar form of blood-poisoning

indicators.note: peculiar suggests the letters of these words are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they will chop away a strange kind of blood-poisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition where toxins circulate in the bloodstream is a type of blood-poisoning.

clue.text: Tried to get the feel of things

definitions.text: Tried to get the feel of things

parts.words: Tried to get the feel of things
parts.note: read literally, this is someone fumbling with their hands to touch what they cannot see

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling about blindly with the hands is searching uncertainly by touch.

clue.text: Space for movement on stage

definitions.meaning: slack or freedom to move, as in a rope or a steering wheel
a drama is what goes on in a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: Slack allowing movement and a drama performed in a theatre share the same word.

clue.text: Split many a framework

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a rack is a framework for holding things

explanation.surface: Lots of racks have split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A split or fissure in a surface is a narrow break.

clue.text: So as to make no bones about it? Just the opposite!

indicators.note: to make here means the letters of so as are rearranged to form another word

explanation.surface: Teases the idiom 'make no bones about it', meaning speak frankly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make no bones' is flipped by 'Just the opposite!': rearranging SO AS does make bones, the Latin plural of os.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a bone is os, and its plural is the anatomical term for skeletal parts.

clue.text: Come back by air

parts.note: not a return flight, but a sound bouncing off a surface and returning through the air

explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound returns to the listener through the air.

clue.text: Comfortable despite having arms raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word for arms reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: arms are weapons such as guns

explanation.surface: Someone is relaxed despite having their arms held up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy and warm, as in a snug little room, is comfortable.

clue.text: Oral inspection arranged whilst dealing with someone else's children

definitions.text: whilst dealing with someone else's children

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of these words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A spoken check is set up while a teacher looks after other people's children.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Latin for 'in the place of a parent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase for acting in place of a parent describes taking responsibility for others' children.

clue.text: Prospecting — hoping to unearth medal?

definitions.meaning: searching the ground for precious metal
a top medal is gold, and digging for one is hoping to unearth it

explanation.definitionFit: Searching for the precious yellow metal, and cryptically excavating for a winner's medal, share the same phrase.
